Source slide page 1 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING MATHEMATICS - I
    Unit - 3: Partial Differential Equations



    Department of Science and Humanities

Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
Contents





 1  P.I. when f(x, y) = xmyn, or a polynomial in  x, y



 2  P.I. when f(x, y) is not of the form eax+by or sin(ax + b) or
   cos(ax + b) or xmyn (a polynomial in x, y)





                                                                                           2 / 11

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
P.I. when f(x, y) = xmyn, or a polynomial in  x, y





 We write the particular integral as

                        z = [F(D, D′)]−1xmyn

We expand [F(D, D′)]−1 as an infinite series and operate on xmyn.  If
F(D, D′) does not contain the constant term, that is, a term independent
 of D and D′, then we expand [F(D, D′)]−1 in powers of (D′)−1D if m < n
and in powers of D−1D′ if m > n





                                                                                           3 / 11

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
Problem




Find the particular integral of the partial differential equation

                       ∂2z −∂2z = x2 + y2
                      ∂x2   ∂y2

Solution: We have [D2 −(D′)2]z = x2 + y2
We write [D2 −(D′)2] = D2 1 −(D−1)2(D′)2

                ∴[D2 −(D′)2]−1 = D−2 1 −(D−1)2(D′)2 −1
   ⇒[D2 −(D′)2]−1 = D−2 1 + (D−1)2(D′)2 + (D−1)4(D′)4 + . . .





                                                                                           4 / 11

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
Problem (contd.)

Therefore, the particular integral is given by

     PI = [D2 −(D′)2]−1(x2 + y2)
      = D−2 1 + (D−1)2(D′)2 + (D−1)4(D′)4 + . . . (x2 + y2)
      = D−2 (x2 + y2) + (D−1)2(D′)2(x2 + y2)
      = D−2 (x2 + y2) + (D−1)2(2)
      = D−2[x2 + y2 + x2]
      = D−2[2x2 + y2]
            x4   x2y2
      =  +         . On integrating twice w.r.t. x
            6     2
We may also write [D2 −(D′)2] = −(D′)2[1 −(D′)−2D2].
In this case, we obtain a different form of the particular integral as
                         z = −y2 [3x2 + y2]
                              6


                                                                                           5 / 11

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
Problem





Find the particular integral of the partial differential equation

     [D2 + 2DD′ + (D′)2]z = 3x + 2y,   or  [D + D′]2z = 3x + 2y

We write
                 [D + D′]2 = [D(1 + D′D−1)]2

and
                 [D + D′]2 = D2(1 + D′D−1)2





                                                                                           6 / 11

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
Problem (contd.)



The particular integral is given by

          z = D−2(1 + D′D−1)−2(3x + 2y)
       = D−2[1 −2D′D−1 + 3(D′D−1)2 −. . .](3x + 2y)
       = D−2[3x + 2y −2D′D−1(3x + 2y)]
       = D−2[3x + 2y −2D′(3x2 + 2xy)]
                                2
       = D−2[3x + 2y −4x]
       = D−2[−x + 2y]
       = −x3 + x2y
                6





                                                                                           7 / 11

Source slide page 8 (extracted text):
Problem (contd.)


We may also write

                [D + D′]2 = [D′(1 + (D′)−1D)]2

The particular integral is given by

     PI = (D′)−2[1 + (D′)−1D]−2(3x + 2y)
      = (D′)−2[1 −2(D′)−1D + 3((D′)−1D)2 −. . .](3x + 2y)
      = (D′)−2[3x + 2y −2(D′)−1D(3x + 2y)]
      = (D′)−2[3x + 2y −2(D′)−1(3)]
      = (D′)−2[3x + 2y −6y]
      = (D′)−2[3x −4y] On integrating twice w.r.t. y
            3xy2 −2y3      =
             2     3

Source slide page 9 (extracted text):
Let f(x, y) be not of any one of the forms as given in the
above cases or the case of failure in Case 2


We use the following procedure:
Assume that F(D, D′) is reducible, that is, it can be factorized. Now
consider one of the factors as

              (a1D + b1D′) z = a1p + b1q = f(x, y).

Since this is a Lagrange’s equation, the auxiliary equations are

                    dx    dy      dz
                =   =                        a1      b1     f(x, y).

The first two ratios give the solution

                  b1 x −a1 y = c,   c arbitrary constant.              (1)





                                                                                           9 / 11

Source slide page 10 (extracted text):
(Contd.)


Consider now the first and third ratios:

              dx      dz             dz
            =      =                               ,
                 a1     f x, y     f x, (b1x −c)/a1

or equivalently
                            h              i                    a1 dz = f x, (b1x −c)/a1 dx.

 Integrating, we get

                 Z       b1x−c
              a1 z =   f x,  a1   dx + c1 = F(x, c) + c1,

where c1 is an arbitrary constant.  After integration, we replace c by
b1x −a1y as given in Eq. 1. Since a particular integral is required, we
 set c1 = 0.




                                                                                          10 / 11

Source slide page 11 (extracted text):
(Contd.)





Therefore,
                          1
                       z =   F x, b1x −a1y
                            a1
We repeat the procedure for each factor to obtain the required
 particular integral.
